evidence_quotes.agenda: 'Do you have any specific concerns or stressors about the moving process in general?' — asked, but only after the full two-location intake was done, right before pricing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A applied — customer said 'no ma'am, my family has moved many times, we're pretty familiar with the process.'
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: Estimate-variability framing with named factors landed clearly ('we also need to consider the factors involved such as the floors and the distance'), but no rate-commit line, no explicit pay-less-if-faster line, no self-prep tip, no 'does that feel fair' check.

top_strength: Patiently managed a very detail-oriented, assertive elderly customer moving his 91-year-old mother between assisted-living facilities, absorbing a lot of unsolicited logistics detail (truck size preferences, distance estimates) without losing control of the call.
coaching_note: The customer pushed back on the time estimate with his own math ('that's four hours at $200, so $800') — the rep confirmed but didn't reinforce it with the pay-less-if-faster framing, which would have been a natural, credible answer to his skepticism about the estimate length.
